picked.t: Inside Binh Tay, the 96-year-old Chinatown market in HCMC
picked.body: Binh Tay Market is situated between Thap Muoi, Le Tan Ke, Phan Van Khoe, and Tran Binh streets in Binh Tay Ward, an area with a large Hoa community, people of Chinese ancestry. Besides serving locals, the market is a regular stop for tourists visiting HCMC. According to Nguyen Thi Ngoc Chau, deputy director of the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market was built in 1930. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. The market, which was renovated in 2016, retains its original architecture. It spreads over 25,000 square meters with a floor area of more than 17,000 square meters, and has one main gate and 12 side entrances. It has a tall tower with four clock faces. The yin-yang tiled roofs are arranged in overlapping layers and curve upward at the corners. In 2017, the market was recognized as a city architectural and artistic heritage site. In 2022, it was named a tourist attraction of HCMC. According to Le Hong Minh, head of the business management team at the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market has 2,358 stalls that sell more than 30 product categories. Its main goods include spices, groceries, clothing, and confectionery. Data from 2023 to 2026 shows that 73% of visitors to the market are international. It receives 120,000 foreign visitors a year, most of them brought on guided tours. On Sept. 8, a group of 10 Indian tourists led by Rohan and his wife spent over an hour exploring the market and buying more than a dozen handmade bags as gifts. Rohan praised its architecture and range of goods but said the products were similar to those at other markets in town. Stalls selling dry goods and spices are located near the market's main gate. Minh said shopping preferences at Binh Tay vary by region. European and American tourists buy handicrafts and clothing. Southeast Asian visitors shop for confectionery, tea, coffee, and bamboo goods. Northeast Asian tourists prefer specialties, dried foods, and herbal medicines. Besides shopping, the market has a food area serving dishes from all over Vietnam. Binh Tay Market plans to combine shopping with cultural and culinary experiences by offering heritage tours, spiritual visits, performances recreating old Chinatown, craft workshops with artisans, and Chinese-Vietnamese cuisine. picked.t: Vietnam has strong potential to attract billions in foreign capital: experts
picked.body: Experts shared these views at the HDBank Global Capital Conference 2026, themed "Global Capital – Vietnam's Aspirations," which brought together nearly 1,000 delegates in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi on Wednesday. Attendees included Philipp Rösler, vice chairman of HD Securities; Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao, chairwoman of Sovico Group; Kim Byoungho, chairman of HDBank; and Darryl James Dong, former head of the International Finance Corporation's (IFC) office in Ho Chi Minh City, along with financial executives, experts and domestic and international investors. Golden opportunity to attract foreign capital Speaking at the conference, Rösler said Vietnam would need approximately $1.5 trillion in investment to achieve double-digit growth from 2026 to 2030, while the state budget could cover only about 20% of the total. This highlights the need to develop domestic capital markets and expand access to international funding. "Capital does not fear risk, but it always fears uncertainty," he said. Capital can move worldwide in search of growth, Rösler said, but stays only where rules are clear, information is transparent and commitments are honored. FTSE Russell's upgrade of Vietnam's stock market and the launch of the Vietnam International Financial Center are complementary milestones. To capitalize on them, he called for consistent and predictable policies, gradual market opening and compliance with international corporate governance standards. From a banking perspective, Kim Byoungho said Vietnam's integration into global financial markets should rest on three pillars: capital, standards and partnerships. HDBank, Sovico and their partners are expanding cooperation in London, New York, Tokyo, Singapore and Seoul to broaden fundraising opportunities and support Vietnamese companies' international expansion. Thomas Nguyen, a senior international stock market expert, said the upgrade would make Vietnam's stock market more accessible to foreign investors. However, attracting global capital remains challenging as much of investors' attention is currently focused on artificial intelligence and technology. He identified four potential drivers of Vietnam's stock market growth in 2027: increased foreign inflows following the upgrade, infrastructure reforms, possible shifts in global capital as the AI investment boom cools, and lower deposit interest rates. Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao said Vietnam's ability to implement programs and projects quickly was a key advantage. She cited the resolution of trading system congestion at the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange within 90 days using domestic technology, and an online platform that raised more than $400 million for the Covid-19 vaccine fund. She also stressed the importance of reliable local partners and regulatory support in investment decisions. Thao said investors who participated in Vietjet's initial public offering (IPO) have seen their investments increase more than fivefold, while those who bought HDBank shares in its 2018 IPO have gained approximately sixfold. She said both companies have maintained commitments to transparency, corporate governance and long-term value creation. Vietnam also has significant investment potential in infrastructure, technology, education, healthcare, culture and human development, she said. "I hope investors, particularly international investors, will seize the opportunities offered by Vietnam's capital market, build a better future for themselves, and grow alongside this market," she added. Gateways connecting Vietnam with global investment markets A highlight of the conference was a bell-ringing ceremony marking the IPO of HD Securities Joint Stock Company (HDS), which has a valuation of nearly $1.8 billion. Representatives of regulators, HDBank and HD Securities joined the ceremony at the HCMC and Hanoi venues. HD Securities Chairman Vu Huu Dien said the company aims to become one of Vietnam's three largest securities firms by 2030 and lead the market in smart trading platforms and AI-powered governance. It also plans to establish a securities subsidiary at the Vietnam International Financial Center. CEO Nguyen Ha Quynh said HD Securities is focusing on four business areas: investment banking, securities brokerage and margin lending, treasury operations, and investment and proprietary trading. The company aims to raise shareholders' equity to VND77-78 trillion ($3 million) by 2030 while maintaining a return on equity above 20%. Its IPO is expected to raise VND4.737 trillion ($183.38 million), with 60% allocated to margin lending, 30% to financial instrument investments and the remainder to other business activities. During a question-and-answer session, Tran Hoai Nam, standing deputy CEO of HDBank, said the bank aims to raise at least $2 billion annually from international sources. picked.t: Nutifood forms US nutrition science alliance with four partners
picked.body: Nutifood announced the establishment of Nutifood American Nutrition Science in Kansas on Nov. 24. The new entity will connect the company's research and product development capabilities with the U.S. nutrition science, dairy ingredients, and manufacturing sectors. The launch was marked by a signing ceremony with Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), witnessed by representatives of the Vietnamese Consulate General in San Francisco and senior U.S. dairy industry executives. Building on a scientific foundation The move builds on Nutifood's more than 25 years of research and development (R&D) experience across Vietnam, Sweden, and Australia, where it has developed nutrition solutions for different consumer needs. In early 2026, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) granted a patent for the company's proprietary FDI formula, expanding its intellectual property portfolio. The U.S. offers an opportunity for Nutifood to tap into an advanced dairy ecosystem spanning ingredients, manufacturing, research, and clinical science. Through its new entity, the company aims to combine its intellectual property and research expertise with U.S. scientific and industrial resources, moving beyond conventional exports to participate more deeply in the nutrition value chain. Four U.S. partners Nutifood is forming a Nutrition Science Alliance with the California Milk Advisory Board (CMAB), California Dairies, Inc. (CDI), DFA, and Natural Immune Systems Laboratories (NIS Labs). Each partner brings different capabilities: CMAB connects the company with California's dairy industry and products bearing the Real California Milk seal; CDI provides large-scale dairy processing and manufacturing; DFA contributes R&D and formula innovation; and NIS Labs offers laboratory testing, preclinical studies, and human research. By combining these capabilities across ingredients, manufacturing, R&D, and clinical research, Nutifood aims to improve control over product development and meet scientific and quality standards in international markets. "Every age group, body condition, and stage of life requires specialized nutrition solutions grounded in scientific evidence. That is why Nutifood American Nutrition Science is not simply looking for ingredient suppliers or manufacturing facilities in the United States," said Tran Bao Minh, vice chairman of Nutifood. "We are building strategic partnerships with CMAB, CDI, DFA, and NIS Labs to combine advanced technology and research capabilities in order to develop new nutrition standards for consumers worldwide." Through its U.S. entity and four strategic partnerships, Nutifood aims to strengthen its international competitiveness by combining its research capabilities and patented technologies with American scientific and manufacturing resources.

기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남의 여권 파워가 세계 85위로 직전 발표 대비 4계단 도약했다. 영국 국제 시민권·영주권 자문회사 헨리앤파트너스(Henley & Partners)가 최근 발표한 '2026년 11월 헨리여권지수(Henley Passport Index)'에 따르면, 베트남의 여권 파워는 세계 85위로 10월 대비 4계단 상승했다. 베트남 여권 소지자는 전 세계 50개국에 무비자 또는 도착비자 형태로 입국이 가능해 코모로와 기니비사우, 요르단과 같은 순위를 나타냈다. 직전 조사와 비교하면 무비자로 입국할 수 있는 국가는 1개 늘었다. 베트남 여권 순위는 올 들어 지속적으로 오르내리는 모습을 보였다. 자세히 살펴보면, 1월 발표에서는 86위를 기록한 뒤, 3월 84위로 2계단 상승했다. 이어 6월 87위, 10월 89위로 약세를 보이더니 이번에 다시 반등했다. 동남아 중에서 베트남은 캄보디아(88위)와 라오스(90위), 미얀마(92위)에 앞섰다. 반면, 싱가포르(1위)와 말레이시아(6위), 브루나이(19위), 태국(64위), 인도네시아(67위), 필리핀(72위)에는 뒤처졌다. 한편, 싱가포르 여권 소지자는 전 세계 193개 목적지에 무비자로 입국할 수 있어 세계에서 가장 강력한 여권 지위를 유지했다. 다음으로는 일본과 아랍에미리트(UAE)가 188개국으로 2위를, 한국은 187개국으로 3위를 차지했다. 여권 순위 최하위 5개국에는 예멘(100위), 파키스탄, 이라크, 시리아, 아프가니스탄(104위)이 포함됐다. 이들 국가 여권 소지자의 무비자 입국 가능국가는 22~30개국에 불과했다. 헨리여권지수는 국제항공운송협회(IATA)의 독점 자료를 바탕으로 전 세계 227개 국가 및 지역의 이동 자유도를 추적, 글로벌 이동 자유도를 나타내는 핵심 지표로, 전체 199개국 여권을 대상으로 사전 비자 없이 입국 가능한 국가 수를 집계해 연중 정기적으로 발표된다.
